items.q: Does Preset Forge work on macOS?
items.a: Yes. Preset Forge runs in any modern browser on macOS, Linux, and Windows. The official Valeton GP-200 editor is Windows-only, so this is the only way to edit GP-200 presets natively on Mac.

items.q: Is Preset Forge an official Valeton tool?
items.a: No. It is an independent, open-source community project. Valeton has not endorsed it. The .prst file format was reverse-engineered from real GP-200 presets.

items.q: Do I need to install anything?
items.a: No. Open the editor in your browser. It runs offline as a Progressive Web App after the first load.

items.q: Can I import Line6 HX Stomp presets?
items.a: Yes. Drop a .hlx file into the editor and Preset Forge converts the signal chain to a GP-200 preset (.prst) entirely in your browser — no upload, no server round-trip.

items.q: How do I sync presets to my GP-200 hardware?
items.a: Connect the GP-200 by USB and use a desktop browser with Web MIDI: Chrome, Edge or another Chromium-based browser, or Firefox 108+ (Safari and mobile browsers are not supported). Preset Forge can read the active preset, send live parameter changes, and write a preset to a specific slot.
Yes. No ads, no paid tier, no account required for browsing or editing. Sharing presets to the public gallery requires a free account.

editorAbout.metaTitle: GP-200 Editor – Free Valeton GP200 Preset Editor | Preset Forge
editorAbout.metaDescription: Free Valeton GP-200 editor in your browser: open and save .prst presets, edit 305 effects and push changes live over USB MIDI. Windows, Mac & Linux.
editorAbout.heading: A free GP-200 editor that runs in your browser
editorAbout.intro: Preset Forge is a free, unofficial editor for the Valeton GP-200 multi-effects pedal. It runs entirely in the browser: there is nothing to download or install, and it works the same on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS. Open a .prst preset, change any effect or parameter and save it again — or connect the GP-200 by USB and hear every change on the pedal as you make it.
editorAbout.whatBody: Every GP-200 preset is a chain of eleven blocks: PRE, WAH, DST, AMP, NR, CAB, EQ, MOD, DLY, RVB, VOL. On the pedal you edit them one at a time on a small screen. In the editor you see the whole signal chain at once, as a pedalboard or as a list. Click a block to pick one of 305 effect models — amps, cabs, drives, modulation, delays, reverbs and more — and set its parameters with knobs, sliders and switches. The effect names and parameter ranges come from Valeton’s own effect list, so the values you set here are the values the pedal uses.
editorAbout.feature1: Load and save .prst files: drag a preset onto the page or pick it from disk, and download your edit as a .prst file again.
editorAbout.feature2: Edit all eleven blocks: switch effects on and off, change the effect type and adjust up to fifteen parameters per block.
editorAbout.feature3: Reorder the signal chain by drag and drop, or with the arrow keys on a focused block header.
editorAbout.feature4: Set the FX loop send and return positions, patch volume, pan and tempo.
editorAbout.feature5: Assign up to three effect parameters each to EXP 1 (modes A and B) and EXP 2, each with its own min/max range.
editorAbout.feature6: Import Line6 HX Stomp .hlx presets and convert them to GP-200 format (experimental).
editorAbout.feature7: With a free account, save presets online, publish them to the community gallery and build playlists for rehearsals and gigs.
editorAbout.liveBody: Connect the GP-200 with a USB cable and click “Connect GP-200”. In Chrome, Edge and other Chromium-based browsers, and in Firefox 108+ on the desktop, the editor talks to the pedal through Web MIDI: switching an effect, turning a knob or reordering the chain is sent to the device instantly. “Load” pulls a whole bank of four presets from the pedal, “Save to [Slot]” writes your preset back, and a .prst file you open while the pedal is connected is sent to it block by block as a live preview. Safari and browsers on iPhone/iPad have no Web MIDI; there you can still edit and save files.
editorAbout.filesBody: The GP-200 stores each preset as a small binary .prst file — 1224 bytes for a user preset. Preset Forge reads and writes this format directly: the preset name and author, all eleven effect blocks with their parameters, and the checksum the pedal verifies. Factory presets open too. Because it is the same file format, you can move between Preset Forge, the official Valeton software and presets you download from other players at any time.
editorAbout.platformsTitle: Windows, Mac, Linux — nothing to install
editorAbout.platformsBody: Valeton’s own GP-200 editor is a Windows desktop application. Preset Forge only needs a browser, so it also runs on a Mac, on Linux distributions such as Ubuntu, Fedora or Mint, and on Chromebooks. After the first visit the editor works offline as a progressive web app (PWA) — handy in a rehearsal room without Wi-Fi.
editorAbout.freeBody: Editing is free and needs no account; an account is only needed to save presets online and share them. The source code is published under the GPL-3.0 licence. Preset Forge is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Valeton.

help.title: Help
help.gettingStartedLoad: Load a .prst file by dragging it into the editor or clicking "Load preset from disk".
help.gettingStartedEdit: Click on an effect slot to adjust parameters. Toggle effects on or off with the LED button. Switch between pedal view and list view.
help.gettingStartedSave: Click "Save preset as file" to download your edited preset as a .prst file.
help.gettingStartedReorder: Drag and drop effect slots to reorder the signal chain — or focus a slot header and press Arrow Up / Arrow Down to move it.
help.gettingStartedAuthor: Each .prst file contains an author name (max 16 characters). You can view and edit it in the editor.
help.hxStompLoad: Load a .hlx file from a Line6 HX Stomp. The app automatically converts it to GP-200 format.
help.hxStompExperimental: This feature is experimental. Not all HX Stomp effects have a GP-200 equivalent — unmapped effects are skipped or approximated.
help.hxStompWhat: Converted presets include effect types, parameters, and signal chain order. Review the result in the editor before saving.
help.usbMidiBrowser: Web MIDI works in Chrome, Edge and other Chromium-based desktop browsers, and in Firefox 108+ on desktop. On first use, Firefox asks you to install a one-time site-permission add-on and then asks for MIDI access. Safari and mobile browsers (including Firefox for Android and all iOS browsers) do not support Web MIDI. Chrome, Chromium and Firefox all run on Linux (e.g. Linux Mint) — Preset Forge is the only GP-200 editor with Linux support.
help.usbMidiConnect: Connect your GP-200 via USB and click "Connect GP-200". The browser will ask for permission to access the MIDI device. Progress is shown live (Identity, Firmware Check, Slot Names).
help.usbMidiLive: Changes in the editor are sent to the device instantly: toggling effects, changing parameters, and reordering the signal chain. The device bar at the top shows the current slot and stays visible while scrolling.
help.usbMidiLoadPush: If the GP-200 is connected when you load a .prst file or a gallery preset, the editor sends the whole preset to the device block by block as a live preview (not saved to a slot). The device bar shows the progress; loading another preset or disconnecting cancels the push in flight.
help.usbMidiPullPush: Use "Load" to pull a preset from the device. Click "Save to [Slot]" to save your changes directly to the device.
help.usbMidiNameEdit: Double-click the preset name in the device bar to rename it directly (max 16 characters).
help.galleryUpload: Sign in and upload presets to your profile. Publish them to the gallery so others can discover them.
help.galleryShare: Each preset gets a unique share link. You can reset the link at any time to revoke access.
help.galleryDownload: Browse the gallery for presets from other users and download them directly. Filter by style or module type.
help.galleryAudio: Add a 30-second audio snippet (MP3 or M4A, max 30 s, max 2 MB) so others can hear your preset — when saving it to your account, or later on its share page.
help.galleryComments: On a preset's share page, signed-in users with a verified email can rate it (1–5 stars) and leave comments. You can't rate your own presets.
help.bankNavTabs: When you load a preset via USB, the entire bank (A/B/C/D) is loaded. Switch between the four slots using the tabs.
help.bankNavPrevNext: Use the arrow buttons on the left and right of the tabs to navigate to the previous or next bank.
help.playlistsCreate: Create playlists with songs for your practice sessions or live performances. Each song can have multiple presets assigned.
help.playlistsSlots: Select device slots from your GP-200 to associate with each preset in a song. Presets are pushed to the device when activated.
help.playlistsCuePoints: Add timed cue points to songs: at a specific timestamp, the app can automatically switch presets or toggle effects on the device.
help.playlistsCountIn: A 3-2-1 count-in is shown before each cue point triggers, so you can prepare for the preset change.
help.playlistsReconnect: If the USB connection drops during a performance, the app will attempt to auto-reconnect without losing your playlist position.
help.shortcutsPlaylistUpDown: Arrow Up / Arrow Down — previous / next song in the playlist player.
help.shortcutsPlaylistLeftRight: Arrow Left / Arrow Right — previous / next preset within the current song.
help.shortcutsEffectReorder: Arrow Up / Arrow Down on a focused effect slot header — move the effect up / down in the signal chain.
help.faqLinuxQ: Does Preset Forge work on Linux (Ubuntu, Fedora, Manjaro, Mint)?
help.faqLinuxA: Yes. Preset Forge runs in the browser on any Linux distribution — Ubuntu, Fedora, Manjaro and Arch, Linux Mint and others (tested on Linux Mint). The GP-200 is a class-compliant USB MIDI device, so Linux needs no driver and no udev rules. For live USB editing use Chrome, Chromium, Brave, Edge or Firefox 108+. If the pedal does not appear, close other programs that use it (a DAW, another tab). Browsers installed as Snap or Flatpak run in a sandbox that may block MIDI access — if so, try your distribution's regular package or the browser vendor's own package. The official Valeton editor has no Linux version.
help.faqLinuxLink: Step-by-step guide: the GP-200 on Linux
help.faqNotDetectedQ: The GP-200 is not detected or it still doesn't work — what can I check?
help.faqNotDetectedA: Go through these steps in order. 1) Use Chrome, Edge, another Chromium-based browser or Firefox 108+ on a computer — Safari and iPhone/iPad browsers have no Web MIDI. 2) Use a USB data cable (charge-only cables carry no MIDI) and switch the GP-200 on before you click "Connect GP-200". 3) Close every other program that may hold the MIDI port: the official Valeton editor, a DAW, MIDI tools or a second Preset Forge tab. 4) Allow MIDI access including SysEx when the browser asks. If you blocked it, re-enable MIDI for preset-forge.com in the site permissions next to the address bar and reload. 5) Unplug the cable, plug it back in, reload the page and connect again. 6) Check the firmware: Preset Forge is tested with firmware 1.8.0.
help.faqWindowsQ: Does it work on Windows 11 and Windows 10?
help.faqWindowsA: Yes. Open the editor in Chrome, Edge or Firefox 108+ and connect the GP-200 by USB — Windows recognises it as a USB MIDI device, and Preset Forge needs no extra software. On Windows a MIDI port can usually be used by only one program at a time, so close the official Valeton editor, your DAW and other MIDI software before you click "Connect GP-200".
help.faqMacQ: Does it work on a Mac?
help.faqMacA: Yes, in Chrome, Edge or Firefox 108+ on macOS. Safari does not support Web MIDI: in Safari you can still load, edit and save .prst files, but live USB editing needs one of the other browsers.
help.faqChromebookQ: Does it work on a Chromebook (ChromeOS)?
help.faqChromebookA: Yes. ChromeOS runs the desktop version of Chrome, which supports Web MIDI with SysEx, so you can load, edit and save presets and connect the GP-200 by USB like on any other computer. Use a USB data cable and allow MIDI access when Chrome asks. Live USB editing on ChromeOS has not been hardware-tested yet — if the pedal does not connect, work through the troubleshooting steps above.
help.faqAndroidA: Partly. You can load, edit and save .prst files in any Android browser, although the editor is designed for larger screens. Live USB editing is not supported on Android: Chrome for Android has Web MIDI and can reach the GP-200 through a USB-OTG adapter, but the connection is unreliable, and Firefox for Android has no Web MIDI at all. For live editing use a computer or a Chromebook.
help.faqIosQ: Does it work on iPhone or iPad?
help.faqIosA: Only for files. On iOS and iPadOS every browser uses Apple's WebKit engine, which has no Web MIDI. You can load, edit and save .prst files, but you cannot connect the GP-200 by USB.
help.faqFirefoxQ: Firefox says Web MIDI requires a site permission add-on — what do I do?
help.faqFirefoxA: That is expected. Firefox (version 108+ on desktop) only enables Web MIDI for a website after you install a small site-permission add-on, which Firefox generates itself for that site. Confirm the installation when Firefox asks, then allow MIDI access. You do this once for preset-forge.com. If you dismissed the prompt, reload the page and click "Connect GP-200" again. Firefox for Android has no Web MIDI.
help.faqLanguagesQ: Is Preset Forge available in other languages?
help.faqLanguagesA: Yes: English, Deutsch, Español, Français, Italiano, Português, Português (Brasil). Change the language with the language switcher in the navigation bar.
help.faqBrowserA: The editor works in all modern browsers (Windows, macOS, Linux). USB MIDI needs Web MIDI: Chrome, Edge and other Chromium-based browsers, or Firefox 108+ on desktop (on first use Firefox installs a one-time site-permission add-on). Safari and mobile browsers are not supported.
help.faqFirmwareA: The app was tested with firmware 1.8.0. Other versions may work but are not officially supported.
help.faqFormatA: The .prst format is the proprietary preset file format of the Valeton GP-200. Each file is exactly 1224 bytes and contains 11 effect slots with up to 15 parameters each.
help.faqOfflineA: Yes — Preset Forge is a PWA and works offline for editing presets. Gallery, profile, and playlist features require an internet connection.
help.faqHxStompQ: Can I import Line6 HX Stomp presets?
help.faqHxStompA: Yes, experimentally. Load a .hlx file in the editor and the app will convert it to GP-200 format. Not all effects have a direct equivalent, so check the result.
help.controllersDesc: Open the Controller panel in the editor and assign up to three effect parameters each to EXP 1 (Mode A and Mode B) and EXP 2. Pick a parameter from the dropdown and set its min/max range (0–100). With the GP-200 connected, changes are sent to the device instantly via USB MIDI.
